name: Fire Magic
oracle_text:
Tiered (Choose one additional cost.)
• Fire — {0} — Fire Magic deals 1 damage to each creature.
• Fira — {2} — Fire Magic deals 2 damage to each creature.
• Firaga — {5} — Fire Magic deals 3 damage to each creature.
blocked_sentences: • Fire — {0} — Fire Magic deals 1 damage to each creature.
• Fira — {2} — Fire Magic deals 2 damage to each creature.
• Firaga — {5} — Fire Magic deals 3 damage to each creature.

needs.what: a card-level additional cost with alternatives -- an `additional_cost_options` list of whole costs (each a cost_keys node, here {"mana": "{0}"}, {"mana": "{2}"}, {"mana": "{5}"}) of which exactly one must be chosen and paid while casting, with the chosen index recorded on the spell so the effect tree can branch on it. That means three parts: the caster picks an option as part of casting (so it is locked in on announcement, is part of the spell's total cost, and raises what an opponent sees paid); the choice binds the effect, either by letting a top-level `choose_mode` mode be selected only when its own option was the one paid, or by a new `condition`/`value` leaf such as `cost_option_chosen` that an `if` can read; and the mode-owned target rule already spelled out for `choose_mode` (a target spec's `mode` index) should keep working, since a tiered mode may target.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `additional_cost` is a single fixed price every cast must pay -- it has no notion of alternatives, so it can express `{2}` or `{5}` but never a choice between them. `additional_optional` is one yes/no price (kicker in disguise) and `kicker`/`multikicker` are the same shape: two outcomes, or N repetitions of one price, not three named tiers at {0}/{2}/{5}, and `multikicker` cannot reach {5} in steps of {2}. `additional_repeatable` likewise multiplies one price. `alternative_cost`, `evoke` and `overload` replace the mana cost rather than add to it, and each offers exactly one alternative. On the effect side `choose_mode` (chooser, count, modes, once_each, or_more, up_to, up_to_if) has no per-mode cost key at all -- writing the three bullets as three free modes would print a {R} instant that deals 3 damage to each creature for one mana, which is strictly cheaper than the card and the exact silent-power-creep failure this pipeline exists to catch. The nearest legal-but-wrong dodge, a nested `may` with `pay` around each damage op, moves the payment to resolution: the tier would be chosen after the spell is on the stack rather than as it is cast, the spell's mana value and total cost paid would be wrong for Trinisphere/Thalia/`additional_paid`-style effects, and the caster could hold the choice open past responses. `additional_paid` can read how much extra was paid but nothing lets a fixed menu of extra prices be offered at cast time, so there is no value for it to read.
